In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

.

Commentary on Surah Al-A'la

It is Meccan.

It is also narrated from al-Dahhak that it is Medinan, but the more correct view is the first, and Allah knows best.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾. That is: magnify your Lord, the Most High. It was also said: declare Him free of imperfection. The glorification of Allah, may His name be exalted, is that He not be described with any description that is not fitting for Him.

Abu Salih narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that its meaning is: pray in obedience to your Lord's command. It was also said: pray to your Lord, the Exalted.

In the verse there is evidence that the name and the named are one, because the meaning is "glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High," and in the recitation of Ubayy it is: "Glory be to your Lord, the Most High."

The poet said:

(Until the year's end, then the greeting upon you both... and whoever weeps for a full year has made an excuse.)

That is: then the greeting upon you both.

Isra'il narrated from Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhita, from his father, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) loved the Surah "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High."

He (al-Sam'ani) said, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Samad al-Tarabi informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamwayh informed us: Ibrahim ibn Khuzaym al-Shashi informed us: 'Abd ibn Humayd informed us: Waki' informed us, from Isra'il, the report.

.

It is narrated in the hadith of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite in the first rak'ah of the witr ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾, in the second: ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾, and in the third: Surat al-Ikhlas and the two protective surahs (al-Mu'awwidhatayn).

It is also narrated from 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar that when they recited ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ they would say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High," in compliance with the command.

[And the better course] is to say it likewise.

[And] it is well known from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir that he said: When the saying of Allah, the Most High, ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Place it in your prostration." And when His saying "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Great" was revealed, he said: "Place it in your bowing."

His saying: ﴿Who created and proportioned﴾. That is: He created you and made you a well-proportioned man.
He is in the sense of His saying: ﴿Who created you, then proportioned you﴾, as we have explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 87, verse 3:

And His words: ﴿Who created and proportioned﴾. Al-Suddi said: "Qadar" means He created the male and the female, and "hada" means: He guided the male to the female.

It is also said: "Qadar" means He created every thing and guided it to what suits it, and this is concerning animals.

It is also said: He guided it to its provision, like the infant who finds the breast and opens its mouth at birth seeking the breast, and the chick seeks provision from its mother and its father, and likewise every thing.

Mujahid said: He guided man to the path of good and evil, and to happiness and misery.

It is also said: there is an omission in the verse, and the meaning is: "and guided and misguided."

And His saying: ﴿And He who brings forth the pasture﴾, meaning: pasture for the cattle.

The poet said:

(And the pasture sometimes grows upon the dung-heaps of the soil... while the grudges of souls remain, just as they are.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 87, verse 5:

And His saying: ﴿So He made it dark-brown stubble﴾ in the verse involves inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) and the meaning is: He brought forth the pasture dark-brown.

﴿So He made it stubble﴾ means: dry.

Al-ghuthaa' (stubble) is what the torrent carries of dry plants and grass, and al-tufat (foam) is what the cooking pot casts off of scum (zabad). Al-ahwa (dark-brown) means black, and al-hawwa (blackness) means blackness (al-sawad).

He called it ahwa (dark-brown) because every green thing inclines toward blackness when its greenness becomes intense.

Dhu al-Rummah said:

(Lamiya's lips carry a dark blackness, a dark-red tint, and in her gums and in her front teeth is a fine whiteness.)

And it is said: He brought forth the pasture green, then He made it dark-brown, then He made it stubble.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 87, verse 6:

His saying: ﴿We shall make you recite, so you will not forget﴾. Ibn Abi Najih mentioned, by his narration from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) "used to move his lips with the recitation of a surah of the Qur'an when Jibril recited it to him, out of fear that it would slip away from him. So Allah, exalted is He, revealed His saying: ﴿We shall make you recite, so you will not forget﴾."

And the meaning is: you have been protected from forgetting, so he did not forget after that.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 87, verse 7:

And His saying: ﴿Except what Allah wills﴾ means: except what Allah wills that you forget. What is meant by this is the abrogation of the recitation (naskh al-tilawa, abrogation in which the recitation is removed). It was also said: forgetting here carries the meaning of leaving, i.e., he will not leave anything except what Allah wills to leave by abrogation.

And it is related from some of them that His saying ﴿Except what Allah wills﴾ mentions the will (mashi'a) as a matter of instruction (ta'lim), so that the word "will" is joined to all of His statements, like His saying: ﴿You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security﴾. He has said: ﴿Except what Allah wills﴾, meaning: that you forget, and He did not will it.

Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Abiding therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, and He did not will it. This was mentioned by Ibn Faris.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud and what is hidden﴾, i.e., the secret and the open, and it is said: what is in the heart and what is on the tongue.
And His saying: ﴿And We will ease you toward ease﴾. Al-Yusra is the feminine form (fu'la, elative-like pattern) of al-yusr (ease), and its meaning is: toward the easier of matters.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 87, verse 9:

And His saying: ﴿So remind, if the reminder benefits﴾. If someone says: how does He say "if the reminder benefits," when he is commanded to remind in general, whether it benefits or not?

The answer has two aspects. The first: the meaning of His saying ﴿if the reminder benefits﴾ is "since the reminder benefits," like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and fear Me, if you are believers﴾, meaning: since you are believers.

.

The second aspect: remind in every case, for the reminder has benefited, so this is a conditional on something certain, and the meaning is: "if it benefits," and it has indeed benefited.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿He who fears will be reminded﴾. It is said: This was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Umm Maktum.

And it is said: It is general, and the meaning is: whoever fears God.

And His saying: ﴿And the most wretched will avoid it, the one who will enter the greatest Fire﴾. It is said: he is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa.

And His saying: ﴿will enter the greatest Fire﴾, meaning: he will enter the greatest Fire.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: it is the lowest level of Jahannam (Hell).

And His saying: ﴿And the most wretched will avoid it, the one who will enter the greatest Fire﴾. It is said: he is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa.

And His saying: ﴿will enter the greatest Fire﴾, meaning: he will enter the greatest Fire.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: it is the lowest level of Jahannam (Hell).

And His words: ﴿Then he will neither die therein nor live﴾ — meaning: he will not die so as to find rest, nor will he live a life in which there is ease. It is also said: he will not die, and he will not find (the spirit/comfort of life).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 87, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Truly he succeeds who purifies himself﴾, meaning: he purifies himself through righteous deeds. It is also said: so-and-so purified himself by saying "There is no god but Allah."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he believed and affirmed the oneness of his Lord.

It is narrated from 'Ata': meaning, he gave the zakat of his wealth.

Ibn Mas'ud said: whoever does not purify himself, his prayer will not be accepted from him.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Umar that it refers to the zakat al-fitr (the charity of breaking the fast at the end of Ramadan).

This is also the view of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz.

Ibn 'Umar used to say to Nafi' when he woke up on the day of the 'Id: "Have you given the zakat al-fitr?" If he said "Yes," he would set out for the prayer; and if he said "No," he would order him to pay it, and then he would set out. This is based on the opinion we stated, that the surah is Medinan. However, if we say it is Meccan, which is the more correct view, then this opinion is not objectionable, because the zakat al-fitr was not obligatory in Mecca; it was made obligatory in Medina, and likewise the 'Id prayer was only performed in Medina.

And His saying: ﴿And remembers the name of his Lord, and prays﴾ — meaning: he remembers his Lord and prays. It is said: the remembrance (dhikr) is the takbir (the saying of "Allahu akbar"), and the prayer (salah) is the well-known prayer. It is also said: it is the Eid prayer.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 87, verse 16:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Rather, you prefer the worldly life﴾, meaning: you choose (it).

Ibn Mas'ud said: "The world was hastened for them, and the Hereafter was hidden from them, so they chose the world over the Hereafter. And when they witnessed the Hereafter, they did not choose anything over it."

Abu Musa al-Ash'ari narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever loves his worldly life harms his Hereafter, and whoever loves his Hereafter harms his worldly life. So prefer what remains over what perishes."
And His saying: ﴿And the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ — i.e., more lasting [and more enduring].

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures﴾, meaning: what Allah has mentioned in this surah. It is also said that it refers to His saying, ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself﴾, up to His saying, ﴿and more enduring﴾. Qatadah said: In all the books of the earlier peoples, [it is stated] that the Hereafter is better and more enduring.

And His saying: ﴿The scrolls of Abraham and Moses﴾, meaning: the books that God Most High sent down to Abraham and Moses. God sent down scrolls (ṣuḥuf) to Abraham, and He sent down the Torah to Moses, so these are what is meant by the verse, and God knows best.
